# Thinking about a heat pump?

A heat pump does not burn fuel to make heat. It moves heat from outside air into your home, even when it feels cold outside.

Because it moves heat instead of making it, a typical heat pump delivers about three units of heat for every unit of electricity it uses. A good gas furnace turns about 90 percent of its fuel into heat.

That does not mean a heat pump always costs less to run. Electricity usually costs more per unit of energy than gas, so the running cost depends on both prices where you live.

How much heat your home needs matters too. Colder winters and draughty homes need more heat, which makes the price difference count for more. Sealing and insulating first can shrink the heat you need, and lets you buy a smaller system.

Efficiency drops in very cold weather. Modern cold-climate models keep working well below freezing, but they make less heat per unit of electricity on the coldest days.

Installation costs vary a lot. Get several quotes, ask about rebates, and check whether your ducts and electrical panel need work.
